critical_code_review_comments: useVoiceIO.speak() correctly wires AnalyserNode AFTER the TTS fetch + BEFORE audio.play(), but the call uses ctx.createMediaElementSource(audio) on a freshly-built <audio> each call. If speak() is called twice in quick succession the previous AudioContext is reused (ttsCtxRef.current) which is fine, but the previous source node is NOT explicitly disconnected — over a long session this can accumulate dangling MediaElementSource nodes. _stopTtsAnalyser disconnects the analyser but not the source. Low-priority leak.

GuidePresence RAF loop (line 106-114) writes --mouth-open every frame even when the value is unchanged. The TODO comment claims a 'skip when unchanged' but no such guard exists. Minor perf nit (60 Hz CSS-var writes are cheap).
BodyRoomChat / ParentsRoomChat voice-status row regression (above) — same code shape as the ClarityRelease block that was cleaned in iter 69. The cleanup needs to be propagated.
useVoiceIO line 565 source.connect(analyser) + analyser.connect(ctx.destination) — correct, this avoids the common 'audio goes silent when you tap an element source' bug.

VAD barge-in (line 360-369): pauses audioRef.current and sets it to null on first voiced frame — works, but does NOT call _stopTtsAnalyser, so the analyser RAF keeps ticking against a now-null audio element for a few frames (sampleLoop has a guard `audio.paused || audio.ended` so it self-fades to 0). Cosmetic, not a bug.
